stops.note: combined 'inuk' (person) and a suffix meaning 'substitute', describing a stone figure that acts in place of a human
stops.meaning: something that acts in the capacity of a human

stops.note: borrowed into English, becoming widely known after being used as the emblem of the 2010 Winter Olympics
stops.meaning: a stone landmark or cairn built by Arctic peoples

current_meaning: a stone landmark or cairn built by Inuit and other Arctic peoples, traditionally used for navigation or communication
